title: Red-black tree
summary: A red-black tree is a self-balancing binary search tree. Each node is red or black. Properties: (1) Every node is red or black. (2) Root is black. (3) Every leaf (NIL) is black. (4) If a node is red, both children are black (no two reds in a row). (5) Every path from root to leaf has the same number of black nodes (black-height). These properties ensure the tree is approximately balanced: height <= 2*log2(n+1).

structure.meaning: Every node is red or black.
If a node is red, both children are black (no two consecutive reds).
Every path from root to leaf has the same number of black nodes.
Left/right rotations rebalance the tree after insert/delete. O(1) per rotation.

notes: Red-black trees are used in the Linux kernel (CFS scheduler, epoll, timer wheel), C++ std::map/set, Java TreeMap.
Red-black trees guarantee O(log n) worst-case for search/insert/delete.
AVL trees are more strictly balanced (height <= 1.44*log2(n)) but require more rotations.
Red-black trees have fewer rotations than AVL (at most 3 per insert, 3 per delete).
Left-leaning red-black trees (Sedgewick) simplify the implementation.
